evidence: The paper develops dynamic prediction models for CLABSI using random forest and XGBoost algorithms. While the RF-ALL model performs "model-driven feature selection, as ranked by the depth in the trees for splitting," no variable importance scores or rankings are reported. All conclusions concern prediction performance: "Among individual models, the XGB-ALL model had the highest AUROC on temporal evaluation, reaching a maximum of 0.748 at landmark 8" and "random forest models showed the best calibration." Clinical utility conclusions reference threshold-dependent decision curves and net benefit metrics, not feature importance rankings or magnitudes.
